chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, your father said: Whoever delays paying its zakat upon it, he must pay it.' He said, 'My father spoke truly; he must pay what was obligatory upon him, and what was not obligatory upon him, there is nothing upon him from it.'

Then he said to me, 'What do you think if a man lost consciousness for a day, then died, and his prayer was missed, would he be obligated to pay it after he died?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'Unless he regained consciousness on that day.'

Then he said to me, 'What do you think if a man fell ill in the month of Ramadan, then died in it, would he be required to fast on his behalf?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'And similarly, a man does not pay from his wealth except what became due upon it.'

And it is not for anyone to say that this interpretation is not possible for you, because the first two narrations included that the questioner asked about jewelry whether zakat is obligatory in it or not, so he said to him, 'No, except what he delayed from the zakat.' And what he makes into jewelry after the time has arrived, zakat is not obligatory in it, but it became obligatory before it became jewelry.

Thus, there is no meaning to excluding some jewelry from the whole, because his saying (peace be upon him) when the questioner asked him about jewelry whether zakat is in it or not, and he said to him, 'No,' necessitates that everything upon which the name of jewelry falls, zakat is not obligatory in it, whether it was crafted before the time arrived or after its arrival, due to its inclusion under the general rule.
So the Imam (peace be upon him) intended by that the specification of some from the whole, and that is what we mentioned earlier, namely what was crafted after the time arrived.

key_terms.تَخْصِيصِ الْبَعْضِ مِنَ الْكُلِّ: Specifying a part from the general whole
key_terms.حُلُولِ الْوَقْتِ: Arrival of the time (completion of the lunar year)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying zakat for gold jewelry that was bought after the zakat year had already passed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the notion of retroactive zakat on gold jewelry by distinguishing between the time of acquisition and the time of obligation (hulul al-waqt). He employs analogies from missed prayers and fasting to demonstrate that financial obligations are tied to the specific period they became due, rather than applying to all possessions indiscriminately. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that zakat is a time-bound duty, ensuring fairness by exempting assets converted to jewelry after the lunar year has passed.
